steps.path: Any file open in the file viewer, in Comments mode
steps.headline: This is what done means for document comments.

rows.statement: Comments are saved in a hidden folder inside the project, beside the app's other hidden project data.
rows.threshold: a hidden project-comments folder holds the saved comment, confirmed on disk

rows.statement: The assistant can reply to your comments.
rows.threshold: asking the assistant to reply posts a reply under the comment, in a dev instance

rows.statement: The assistant can resolve a comment once it finishes what you asked.
rows.threshold: the assistant resolves the comment it acted on, in a dev instance

rows.statement: The assistant can leave its own comments on your document.
rows.threshold: the assistant adds a comment of its own, in a dev instance

rows.statement: The assistant can edit your file to fix what a comment asks, under its usual edit approval rules.
rows.threshold: asking the assistant to fix a comment produces an edit through normal approval, in a dev instance

rows.statement: On the phone, tapping a highlight opens the comment list, the same as clicking it does on desktop.
rows.threshold: tapping a highlight on a phone-sized screen opens the comment list, in a dev instance

rows.statement: The July "Ask Claude about this" draft pull request is closed, with a note pointing to this work.
rows.threshold: PR #263 shows as closed on GitHub, with a note linking here

rows.statement: Comments appear as highlights in the file; hovering one shows a card to reply or resolve, and clicking opens the panel.
rows.threshold: hovering, replying, resolving and clicking a highlight all work, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Selecting text or right-clicking opens the same menu; choosing Add comment opens a small box by the selection.
rows.threshold: selecting text and right-clicking open one shared menu with Add comment, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Show Resolved sits at the top of the comment panel, under the title.
rows.threshold: Show Resolved appears at the top of the panel, under the title

rows.statement: The comment panel has a close button in its top right corner.
rows.threshold: a close control sits in the panel's top right corner

rows.statement: Ask about this adds a chip to your message; hovering or clicking it shows or scrolls to its source, even after sending.
rows.threshold: the chip highlights and scrolls to its source before and after sending, in a dev instance

rows.statement: The Ask Your Assistant and Edit buttons are opaque and clearly clickable, matching every other button in the app.
rows.threshold: both buttons look solid and clickable, matching the app's other buttons

rows.statement: Word and spreadsheet files use the same comment panel; colleagues' Word comments show their name, and commented cells get a red corner mark.
rows.threshold: opening a real Word file and spreadsheet shows comments and marked cells, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Code files use the same comment panel, and Ask about this chips made from code highlight their lines.
rows.threshold: a code file's comments and chips highlight the right lines, in a dev instance

rows.statement: On the Projects screen, Comments appears as a header button beside the file's other actions, opening the same panel.
rows.threshold: the Projects screen's Comments button opens the same comment panel, in a dev instance

rows.statement: On a phone, tapping a highlight or commented cell slides that comment up from the bottom.
rows.threshold: tapping a highlight or commented cell on a phone-sized screen slides the comment up, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Sending comments to Ask Your Assistant from Projects opens the most recent chat in that file's project, or starts a new one.
rows.threshold: sending from Projects opens or reuses the file's project chat, in a dev instance with multiple chats

rows.statement: The three rejected practice branches and folders are deleted from GitHub and this computer.
rows.threshold: the three branches and folders no longer exist, on GitHub and locally
